reliability.rationale: The selected utilization rule improves mean system error over generic controls (77726.8 versus 86915.3 tokens/s RBF), but simpler workload-only models win retrospectively and confirmation error greatly exceeds development. Claim-specific conclusion: A compact calibrated utilization predictor transfers to the reserved system set, with substantial residual error and workload dependence.

mechanism.rationale: A logistic utilization association does not identify coordination overhead. Accelerator count, software, precision and workload are confounded. Eight development rows have Server above Offline, so the logistic upper bound is a model restriction, not a certified physical ceiling.

novelty.rationale: Known source analysis and established equation families are disclosed. No exhaustive novelty adjudication or independent experimental replication is claimed.

significance.rationale: Useful calibrated Offline-to-Server transfer benchmark with substantial scale extrapolation limitations.

reproducibility.rationale: Inspected task, equations, units, source audit, native preparation and compact evidence. Complete numerical replay belongs to the separate computational review.

impact.rationale: No independent deployment, intervention, economic saving or operational safety outcome was measured.
